minutes.headline: Voters killed the $110k Hickory Hills PFAS pilot study article after lake residents objected; other articles went ahead.
minutes.summary: At the annual Water District meeting, voters took up the reports, operating budget, short-term borrowing authority and several water enhancement account appropriations. The PFAS pilot study for the Hickory Hills well drew extended opposition from lake residents who wanted an agreement on withdrawals first, and the article was voted down. Outcomes of the other votes are mostly not stated in the captions.

public_comment.topic: Asked whether the operating budget includes money for the Hickory Hills well; told no.
Questions on the revenue anticipation borrowing: what it is for, whether it has been used, and any fees.
Asked about security of the SCADA control panel against cyber attack and third-party access.
Asked about hard water, calcium and clogged showers, and asked for notification to residents about the well flow change.
Read from 1994 pumping test report arguing the lake would be affected; urged voting down the PFAS study until an agreement with the lake association exists.
Former lake association president said the lake had not been consulted and the district's meetings are poorly attended.
Concern about future commercial use of the well and need for an agreement before the study.
Urged the district to withdraw the article and negotiate a plan with Hickory Hills first, saying many lake residents would turn out.
Said the district knows how to reach him and disputed claims that contact was impossible.
Ratepayer opposed spending on a study of a well without community approval.

what_happened.line: Voters at the Water District annual meeting defeated the article for an engineering pilot study of PFAS treatment at the Hickory Hills well.
Lake residents urged a no vote until an agreement with the lake association exists; the moderator kept debate to the study itself.
Several water enhancement account appropriations were taken up: main repair, a utility vehicle, a SCADA server, and a pump at well station five.
Voters took up the FY2023 operating budget and the authority to borrow short term against revenue; the captions do not state the outcomes.
Staff said they would try a higher flow rate at a well to reduce water hardness and review treatment later.

why_it_matters: The PFAS study vote decides whether the district gets engineering advice on treating the Hickory Hills well, which bears on future drinking water supply and treatment costs for ratepayers.
Residents asked for notice about the well flow change, and the district's dealings with the lake over withdrawals remain unsettled, which bears on any future article on this well.
watch_next: Whether the district negotiates an agreement with the Hickory Hills lake association and brings the PFAS study back to voters.
